note: Curated catalogue. Coordinates marked 'rover_waypoint' are taken from the official Mars 2020 traverse (measured); others are read from published maps (+/-300 m). Scientific descriptions are literature interpretations and may be revised.

targets.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
targets.summary: Perseverance touchdown site (18 Feb 2021) on the crater-floor Máaz formation, ~2 km SE of the western delta front. Flat, low rock abundance; demonstrated safe landing terrain.
targets.science_value: Reference ground truth for crater-floor lavas (Máaz fm.) and for calibrating orbital terrain products.
sources: Farley, K.A. et al. (2022) Science 377, eabo2196

targets.name: Séítah
targets.summary: Olivine-rich cumulate unit (Séítah formation) forming a rugged, ripple-covered low; sampled by Perseverance (Salette, Coulettes, Robine, Malay cores).
targets.science_value: Igneous crater-floor rocks altered by water (carbonate, sulfate, perchlorate detected). Key for radiometric dating of the crater floor.

targets.name: Three Forks sample depot
targets.summary: Flat area at the base of the delta where Perseverance deposited 10 sealed sample tubes (Dec 2022 - Jan 2023) as a backup cache for Mars Sample Return.
targets.science_value: Logistics landmark; terrain proven benign for rover operations and tube deposition.
sources: NASA/JPL (2023) Perseverance sample depot press release

targets.name: Hogwallow Flats / Wildcat Ridge
targets.summary: Fine-grained sandstones and mudstones at the delta front (Shenandoah formation) with the highest organic signal detected by SHERLOC so far; sulfate-rich.
targets.science_value: Top astrobiology target: fine-grained lacustrine/deltaic sediments with aromatic organics and sulfates.

targets.name: Kodiak butte
targets.summary: Isolated delta remnant south of the main fan showing textbook Gilbert-type topset/foreset/bottomset stratigraphy, imaged from Van Zyl Overlook.
targets.science_value: Proved that Jezero hosted a lake with a stable water level (~ -2490 m) and later high-energy floods.

targets.name: Delta top (Berea / Ouzel Falls)
targets.summary: Coarse conglomerates and sandstones of the upper delta (Tenby formation) recording river floods that transported boulders from the Neretva watershed.
targets.science_value: Samples of the catchment lithologies and fluvial energy history; carbonate-cemented sandstones.

targets.name: Marginal carbonate unit
targets.summary: Mg-carbonate and olivine bearing unit along the inner western crater margin ('Margin Unit'), interpreted as a possible lake-shoreline deposit or altered volcanic unit.
targets.science_value: Carbonates can preserve biosignatures and record ancient atmospheric CO2; strongest orbital carbonate signature in Jezero.

targets.name: Bright Angel (Cheyava Falls)
targets.summary: Light-toned outcrop in Neretva Vallis where the 'Cheyava Falls' rock showed leopard-spot reduction halos, organics and phosphate - a potential biosignature candidate.
targets.science_value: Highest-priority astrobiology sample (Sapphire Canyon) of the mission to date.
sources: Hurowitz, J.A. et al. (2025) Nature (Cheyava Falls)
NASA/JPL (2024) 'Perseverance finds rock with potential biosignature'

targets.name: Neretva Vallis (inlet channel)
targets.summary: Western inlet valley that fed the Jezero paleolake and built the western delta; ~ 1 km wide breach of the crater rim.
targets.science_value: Fluvial transport pathway; exposes rim/watershed lithologies and channel-fill sediments.
sources: Goudge, T.A. et al. (2015) JGR Planets 120, 775

targets.name: Sava Vallis (northern inlet)
targets.summary: Second inlet valley entering Jezero from the north with a smaller fan deposit.
targets.science_value: Comparative fluvial system; smaller northern delta remnant.

targets.name: Pliva Vallis (outlet channel)
targets.summary: Eastern outlet channel that breached the rim, proving the paleolake overflowed (open-basin lake).
targets.science_value: Constrains the maximum lake level and overflow history.
sources: Fassett, C.I. & Head, J.W. (2005) GRL 32, L14201

targets.name: Lookout Hill / Witch Hazel Hill (crater rim)
targets.summary: Crater rim crest reached in Dec 2024 after a ~500 m climb; Witch Hazel Hill exposes layered Noachian rim rocks and impact breccias.
targets.science_value: Oldest materials accessible: pre-Jezero crust and impact melt; also the steepest terrain the rover has driven.

targets.name: Belva crater
targets.summary: ~0.9 km impact crater punched into the delta, exposing a natural cross-section of delta strata in its walls.
targets.science_value: Vertical exposure of the delta's internal architecture.

targets.name: Crater floor fractured rough unit
targets.summary: Olivine/pyroxene-bearing fractured unit covering the central crater floor; dark, fractured surface with eolian bedforms.
targets.science_value: Possible volcanic flow or airfall deposit postdating the lake; datable surface.
sources: Stack, K.M. et al. (2020) Space Sci. Rev. 216, 127
